questions.question: Day 14 Practice (Clinic & Pharmacy Visits (Phase 2)): When talking about inquiring about doctor appointment (twice a week), which sentence is grammatically correct for 'My manager'?

options.a: I am inquiring about doctor appointment right now.
options.b: I need to consult a doctor regarding a mild fever.
options.c: Doctor meeting wanted for fever.
options.d: Doctor meeting wanted for fever. yesterday

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
Natural everyday English uses standard tense agreement: "I need to consult a doctor regarding a mild fever.".

questions.question: Day 14 Vocabulary (Clinic & Pharmacy Visits (Phase 2)): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'hedge against'?

options.a: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.
options.b: Protect against potential financial or operational loss.
options.c: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.
options.d: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
'hedge against' means: protect against potential financial or operational loss. Example: "We must diversify to hedge against market risk."

questions.question:
Day 14 Translation Scenario 1 (Clinic & Pharmacy Visits (Phase 2)):

Telugu: "ముందుగా సమస్య యొక్క మూలకారణాన్ని కనుగొనాలి."
(Literal attempt: "First problem root cause finding wanted.")

options.a: First problem root cause finding wanted.
options.b: First and foremost, we must identify the root cause of the issue.
options.c: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.d: I am needing to first problem root cause finding wanted.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
Natural Version: "First and foremost, we must identify the root cause of the issue."

Use 'First and foremost' and 'identify the root cause'.

questions.question:
Day 14 Translation Scenario 2 (Clinic & Pharmacy Visits (Phase 2)):

Telugu: "అన్నా, బస్టాండ్ దగ్గర డ్రాప్ చేయండి, ఎంత అవుతుంది?"
(Literal attempt: "Brother bus stand drop me, how much will become?")

options.a: Please drop me off near the bus stand. How much is the fare?
options.b: I am needing to brother bus stand drop me, how much will become?
options.c: Brother bus stand drop me, how much will become?
options.d: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option A
Natural Version: "Please drop me off near the bus stand. How much is the fare?"

Avoid 'how much will become' and ask 'How much is the fare?'.

questions.question:
Day 14 Translation Scenario 3 (Clinic & Pharmacy Visits (Phase 2)):

Telugu: "ఈ టమాటాలు కేజీ ఎంత? కొంచెం తాజావి ఏరి ఇవ్వండి."
(Literal attempt: "These tomatoes kg how much? Pick give fresh.")

options.a: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.b: I am needing to these tomatoes kg how much? pick give fresh.
options.c: How much are these tomatoes per kilo? Please pick out fresh ones for me.
options.d: These tomatoes kg how much? Pick give fresh.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option C
Natural Version: "How much are these tomatoes per kilo? Please pick out fresh ones for me."

Use 'per kilo' for price and 'pick out' for selection.

questions.question:
Day 14 Translation Scenario 4 (Clinic & Pharmacy Visits (Phase 2)):

Telugu: "నాకు కొంచెం తలనొప్పిగా ఉంది, ఒక గంట సేపు రెస్ట్ తీసుకుంటాను."
(Literal attempt: "To me little headache is there, take rest one hour.")

options.a: I am needing to to me little headache is there, take rest one hour.
options.b: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.c: I have a slight headache; I'm going to rest for an hour.
options.d: To me little headache is there, take rest one hour.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option C
Natural Version: "I have a slight headache; I'm going to rest for an hour."

Say 'I have a slight headache' instead of literal translations.
